articles.headline: Giants' Jameis Winston 'lets the dogs out' on 4th down; Commanders don't bite
articles.description: Giants quarterback Jameis Winston broke into a rendition of "Who Let the Dogs Out" in an attempt to draw the Commanders offside on fourth down in New York's 24-21 loss.
articles.headlineJa: ジャイアンツのジェイミス・ウィンストンが4ダウンで「犬を放つ」も、コマンダースはかからず
articles.descriptionJa: ジャイアンツのクォーターバック、ジェイミス・ウィンストンは、24-21で敗れた試合の4ダウン時に、コマンダースをオフサイドに誘い出そうと曲「Who Let the Dogs Out」を口ずさんだ。
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- Jameis Winston dipped into his bag of tricks and barked out an unlikely chant for a key situation in a 24-21 loss for the New York Giants on Thursday night against the Washington Commanders.

Winston went to the line of scrimmage on a critical fourth-down play late in the fourth quarter and yelled the lyrics to the famous song by the Baha Men "Who Let the Dogs Out," which was also a signature chant for New York Knicks coach Mike Brown during his team's championship run in the spring.

"Who let the dogs out?" Winston screamed at the line of scrimmage. "Who! Who!"

The latter part was done emphatically in an attempt to force the Commanders to jump offsides -- they did not. The Giants took a 5-yard penalty and punted with 3:27 remaining.

"Trying to get them offsides," Winston said of the play.

This was something the Giants had practiced. They put time and effort into using the song's hook as their cadence.

It was their unique but unsuccessful attempt to draw a key penalty on Washington.

"Just practicing that with the team," Winston said of the unusual cadence. "The defenses are trying to jump the rhythm. Came up with that. Wish we could've got them to jump offsides."

Winston, known for his gregarious personality, came up with the idea to use the song for the situation. How did he land on "Who let the dogs out?"

"Just had a nice ring to it," he said.

It was fourth-and-1 from the Giants' 11-yard line when coach John Harbaugh had his offense run back on the field in an attempt to make it look like they would go for the knockout punch. New York held a 21-17 lead with just over three minutes remaining.

But Harbaugh wasn't seriously thinking about going for the first down so deep in his own territory.

"I thought maybe we could draw them offsides, get them to jump, you know," he said. "Took a shot at it. They didn't do it. Played with good discipline there."

Harbaugh said he was aware that the unpredictable and charismatic Winston was going with the "Who Let the Dogs Out" chorus in that instance.

"Yeah, I knew that," Harbaugh said. "That was part of the cadence there. That was part of the cadence. Teams do jump in those situations sometimes. That was the idea."

Quarterbacks have long used different words, phrases or songs for their cadences. Hall of Famer Peyton Manning famously used "Omaha." Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott has long said, "Here we go!" at the line of scrimmage.

Winston just might need a little refresher course on "Who Let the Dogs Out." He credited the Black Eyed Peas, not the Baha Men, as the song's artists.

Now, as a cadence on the football field, it will be credited to him.

articles.headline: Cade Cunningham's historic night puts Pistons past Wizards in 2OT thriller
articles.description: Cade Cunningham had 52 points, 11 assists and no turnovers as the Pistons outlasted the Wizards in double overtime Thursday night.
articles.headlineJa: ケイド・カニンガムの歴史的な夜、ピストンズが2OTの接戦でウィザーズを撃破
articles.descriptionJa: 木曜夜のダブルオーバータイムの激闘で、ケイド・カニンガムが52得点11アシスト、ターンオーバーなしという驚異的な成績を残し、ピストンズがウィザーズを破った。
articles.body:
WASHINGTON -- The Wizards kept making last-second shots, forcing Cade Cunningham to play an extra 10 minutes.

All that did was turn a great night into a historic one for the Detroit Pistons star.

Cunningham scored 52 points and had 11 assists, leading Detroit to a 144-140 win in double overtime Thursday night. He became the first player since at least 1978 with at least 50 points and 10 assists in a game with no turnovers. In a game that was mostly tight throughout, Cunningham kept mistakes to a minimum while still being incredibly productive.

"It was the best I've ever done it in my NBA career for sure," Cunningham said.

Cunningham had only 22 points after three quarters before scoring 18 in the fourth. That still wasn't enough because Trae Young's 3-pointer at the buzzer tied the score at 121. Then Washington scored the first seven points of overtime, but there was still plenty of time for Cunningham. A jumper, two free throws and a 3-pointer later, he'd tied the score at 130.

Duncan Robinson put the Pistons ahead with a jumper, but AJ Dybantsa -- the top pick in this year's draft -- tied it with less than a second left for Washington.

There were four players in this game who were picked No. 1 -- Dybantsa, Anthony Davis, Deandre Ayton and Cunningham. Davis had 30 points and 15 rebounds for the Wizards before fouling out in the second overtime after Cunningham made a 3 to put the Pistons up 135-132.

Young scored 37 points and Alex Sarr had 30. The Wizards had not had three 30-point scorers in a game since Nov. 18, 1969, when the team was called the Baltimore Bullets and Mike Davis, Earl Monroe and Gus Johnson formed the high-scoring trio against the San Diego Rockets.

Cunningham equaled the fourth-highest scoring total in franchise history for the Pistons. Jerry Stackhouse scored 57 points in a 2001 game, Kelly Tripucka had 56 in 1983, Dave Bing had 54 in 1971 and George Yardley scored 52 in 1958.

But the statistical feats didn't stop there for Cunningham.

• He became the fifth player with a 50-point double-double and zero turnovers in a game since 1977-78, joining Michael Jordan (twice), Moses Malone, Carmelo Anthony and Giannis Antetokounmpo.

• He became the third Pistons player with a 50-point double-double, joining Yardley (twice in 1957-58) and Blake Griffin (2018-19).

• He scored 30 points in the fourth quarter and overtime, the most by a Pistons player in the play-by-play era (since 1997-98).

Down the stretch, Cunningham took over, even overshadowing teammate Ausar Thompson's first career triple-double.

"He led us through the fourth quarter and overtimes," said Thompson, who had 17 points, 11 assists and 11 rebounds. "He did what he does. One person can't just guard him."

Information from ESPN Research and The Associated Press was used in this report.

articles.headline: Commanders keep NFC East hopes alive with win over Giants
articles.description: New York couldn't close out a win against Washington, giving up a late touchdown drive. Its division lead is now shrinking.
articles.headlineJa: コマンダースがジャイアンツに勝利し、NFC東地区の望みを繋ぐ
articles.descriptionJa: ニューヨークは終盤にタッチダウンを許し、ワシントン戦での勝利を逃した。これにより、地区首位のリードが縮まっている。
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- The Washington Commanders might have saved their season Thursday night. If nothing else, the Commanders extended the belief that they can contend for the NFC East title.

Washington's comeback 24-21 win against the New York Giants improved its record to 3-5-1. Now, the Commanders are two games behind New York while owning the tiebreaker. They have more work to do to climb back into the race, but the win staved off questions about Dan Quinn's coaching future.

If they had lost Thursday, they would have been all but eliminated -- and Quinn's job security would have become a primary topic considering they entered the game 7-17-1 since the start of last season. It was the first time Washington won by scoring a touchdown on its final drive. The Commanders had been 1-3-1 in games decided by a touchdown or less before Thursday.

Here are the most important things to know for both teams:

Washington Commanders (3-5-1)

What to make of Daniels' performance: Jayden Daniels overcame his first two interceptions of the season and delivered when Washington needed him most. His strength has been shaking off bad plays, and after consecutive series ended with picks in the fourth quarter, he led the go-ahead touchdown drive -- with a 32-yard touchdown pass to Stefon Diggs. Daniels had been highly efficient prior to that pass. He has gotten better at keeping his eyes downfield, which resulted in one play for 30 yards.

Trend to watch: Washington's defense has forced six turnovers in its past three games combined. The Commanders now have 14 takeaways this season, but none was bigger than corner Rasul Douglas' interception to end the Giants' final possession. Washington forced a fumble in the red zone, preventing a potential field goal if nothing else.

Most surprising performance: Tight end Ben Sinnott. He entered with one reception on the season, a disappointing total for the 2024 second-round pick. He was supposed to get more action in Washington's new scheme this season, but it took until Week 10 for him to play a bigger role. He caught four passes for 42 yards and a touchdown against the Giants. -- Keim

Next game: vs. Cincinnati Bengals (Nov. 23, at 8:15 p.m. ET)

New York Giants (5-3-1)

The Giants had a chance to all but bury the NFC East by beating the Commanders. They came up just short by allowing Washington to go 71 yards in 49 seconds late in the fourth quarter and throwing a late interception that ended the game. Now, the division is back open.

The Commanders have life. The door is open for the Dallas Cowboys, who play the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday. The Giants entered Thursday night with a 2.5-game lead in the division. A victory would have made them 3-0-1 with wins over each team in the division. They just couldn't finish this one, even with quarterback J.J. McCarthy playing one of the best games of his career up until coming up short in the final seconds.

What to make of McCarthy's performance: Another strong performance

articles.headline: Jayden Daniels and Commanders rally to stun the Giants 24-21 and keep their hopes alive
articles.description: — Even after Jayden Daniels threw two interceptions and it looked like the Washington Commanders were hurtling toward a painful loss at the New York Giants, teammates remembered what it was like when the franchise quarterback burst onto the scene in...
articles.headlineJa: ジェイデン・ダニエルズとコマンダースが反撃、ジャイアンツを24-21で破り望みを繋ぐ
articles.descriptionJa: ジェイデン・ダニエルズが2つのインターセプトを投げ出し、ワシントン・コマンダースがニューヨーク・ジャイアンツに痛い敗戦を喫するかと思われたが、チームメイトたちは、このフランチャイズのクォーターバックが華々しく登場した時のことを思い出していた……。
articles.body:
EAST RUTHERFORD, N.J. -- — Even after Jayden Daniels threw two interceptions and it looked like the Washington Commanders were hurtling toward a painful loss at the New York Giants, teammates remembered what it was like when the franchise quarterback burst onto the scene in 2024 and led some memorable comebacks in a magical rookie year.


              “We felt it,” tight end Ben Sinnott said. “Being able to get another opportunity with the ball in our hands to go win it, it definitely took me back to that season.”


              Daniels delivered, making up for his first two interceptions this year by connecting with Stefon Diggs on a go-ahead, 32-yard touchdown with 57 seconds left to complete a 24-21 victory Thursday night in what was essentially a must-win game.


              “You could mess up the whole game but still have a chance to win,” said Daniels, who was 23 of 33 for 249 yards and also had TD throws to Sinnott and Antonio Williams while running 10 times for 28 yards.


              Coming back keeps hope alive for the Commanders (3-5-1), who moved two games back of the NFC East-leading Giants (5-3-1) and now own the tiebreaker after the teams tied last month. 


              “It just gives you confidence we can go out there and compete and we can close out a game versus the top dog,” Daniels said. “Last time we played them it didn’t go the way that we wanted to or planned to, so we went out there and we improved from the last time. We responded when we had those moments.”


              Daniels getting picked off by Jevon Holland on his 208th pass attempt and Ar'Darius Washington on his 211th looked like it would haunt Washington, which allowed J.J. McCarthy and Isaiah Likely to hook up for a 66-yard, go-ahead TD midway through the fourth quarter and saw Cam Skattebo run into the end zone twice.


              But the Giants were unable to move the ball effectively enough on the ground to run the clock. One QB sneak by Winston was originally called a first down, but coach Dan Quinn challenged it and it got reversed.


              Defensive lineman Deatrich Wise was adamant about Winston not getting it, simply, “Because I stopped him.”


              Winston tried to get the Commanders to jump offside with a hard count of “Who Let the Dogs Out” — with a series of barks — but that did not work and New York kept giving Daniels the ball back by punting the ball multiple times.


              “It’s a missed opportunity, certainly, but it doesn’t change things for us,” coach John Harbaugh said. “There is still a lot of football to play. We played well — just not well enough. We worked hard for this, but you can’t let it bring you down. This was one that got away.”

articles.headline: Booker scores 30 as Suns hold on to beat Hornets 101-96 in Bridges' first game against Charlotte
articles.description: — Devin Booker had 30 points, seven assists and three steals, and the Phoenix Suns beat the Charlotte Hornets 101-96 on Thursday night.
articles.headlineJa: ブッカーが30得点し、サンズがホーネッツに101-96で勝利。ブリッジズにとって初のシャーロット戦に
articles.descriptionJa: デビン・ブッカーが30得点、7アシスト、3スティールを記録し、フェニックス・サンズが木曜夜にシャーロット・ホーネッツを101-96で破った。
articles.body:
PHOENIX -- — Devin Booker had 30 points, seven assists and three steals, and the Phoenix Suns beat the Charlotte Hornets 101-96 on Thursday night. 


              Miles Bridges got the win in his first meeting against his former team as the Suns won for the fourth time in five games after a 1-5 start. Dillon Brooks added 15 points and Collin Gillespie had 13 for the Suns.


              Bridges finished with 11 points and six rebounds. The No. 12 pick in the 2018 draft spent his first seven seasons in Charlotte, where he is third in team history in points, before being dealt to Phoenix in a deal that sent Grayson Allen and Royce O’Neale to the Hornets.


              Coby White scored 21 points and Naz Reid had 16 for shot 6 for 18 from the field for the Hornets. Allen had 14 points and Christian Anderson finished with 13. 


              Booker's 3-pointer gave Phoenix a 97-91 lead with 28 seconds left but O'Neale converted a four-point play that cut it to two. Bridges made two free throws and Booker added two more after a steal as the Suns held on.


              Booker scored 13 points as Phoenix took a 28-22 lead after one quarter, and the Suns extended it to 48-31 when Bridges capped a 15-4 run with a layup midway through the second. Charlotte closed well and cut it to 55-50 at halftime on Allen's 3-pointer. 


              Up next
              Hornets: Visit the Los Angeles Clippers on Sunday.


              Suns: Host the Los Angeles Lakers on Sunday.


              ------

articles.headline: Timberwolves rout the Mavericks 133-94 for their most lopsided win of the season
articles.description: — LaMelo Ball made six 3-pointers and finished with 22 points and a season-high nine assists, and the Minnesota Timberwolves beat the Dallas Mavericks 133-94 on Thursday night for their most lopsided victory of the season.
articles.body:
MINNEAPOLIS -- — LaMelo Ball made six 3-pointers and finished with 22 points and a season-high nine assists, and the Minnesota Timberwolves beat the Dallas Mavericks 133-94 on Thursday night for their most lopsided victory of the season.


              Bones Hyland scored 24 points off the bench to lead the Timberwolves, who won their fifth straight game. Ayo Dosunmu added 18 points, Jaden McDaniels had 16 and Jonathan Kuminga had 14 points and eight rebounds.


              Minnesota shot 61% in the first half to build a 15-point advantage, then blew it open by outscoring Dallas 36-17 in the third quarter to open a 103-69 lead. 


              Zaccharie Risacher scored 22 points off the bench for the Mavericks, who had their three-game winning streak snapped. Cooper Flagg, who had 43 against Indiana in his last game, was held to 12 points and Kyrie Irving had just 10.


              The Wolves beat the Mavs for the seventh straight time and did it easily. Their previous largest margin of victory in a game this season was 25 points and their 44-point lead in the fourth quarter was their biggest at any point this season.


              Ball scored 16 points in the first half and Hyland came off the bench to make all three 3-pointers as Minnesota took a 67-52 lead to the break. A 17-4 surge out of the locker room extended it to 84-56 when Ball threw an alley-oop pass to Rudy Gobert.


              Naji Marshall scored 13 points for Dallas, which shot 37%.


              Up next
              Mavericks: Visit Cleveland on Saturday.


              Timberwolves: Host Chicago on Saturday.


              ------

articles.headline: NFL Week 10 uniforms: Titans debut Rivalries look, Ravens go all-black
articles.description: Here's a look at what each NFL team is wearing in Week 10, led by the Tennessee Titans' Rivalries look.
articles.body:
The NFL regular season has officially passed the halfway point, meaning we are approaching the final chances to see threads on the field. Thankfully, the uniform heat isn't stopping any time soon as alternates continue to make headlines around the league. This week, it's the Tennessee Titans' turn as they debut their Rivalries look.

Tennessee will wear its "Music City"-inspired combination against the Jacksonville Jaguars. It includes a two-tone blue color palette with a Titans-blue lid and navy uniform. The numbers are reminiscent of a neon sign, a nod to those that run through Nashville. "Music City" runs across the chest, while six rhythmic stripes run down the side, similar to strings on a guitar. 

It's a fresh look for the Baltimore Ravens, too, who will debut their all-black combination against the Los Angeles Chargers on "Monday Night Football." The headline for Baltimore's threads is a new matte black lid, nicknamed the "Darkness Helmet." It includes black talon stripes and a two-toned Ravens logo that features red eyes. The shield shoulder patch is black and midnight purple, while "darkness there and nothing more" runs on the inside collar -- a reference to a quote from Edgar Allen Poe's "The Raven."

Monochromatic alternates are popular around the rest of the league. The Cincinnati Bengals will wear their "White Bengal" helmet with all-white uniforms, first introduced in 2022, against the Pittsburgh Steelers. Cincinnati has gone 5-1 in the white helmets since they debuted in 2022. The New York Jets are rocking the "Legacy Black" threads against the Buffalo Bills, while the New Orleans Saints will also go all-black against the Carolina Panthers. It's "Alpha Dawg" week for the Cleveland Browns, who will don all-brown against the Houston Texans.

Fans of nostalgia aren't leaving empty-handed. The San Francisco 49ers are wearing their red 1994 throwback threads against the Dallas Cowboys on the road for a classic uniform matchup. Thursday night had the New York Giants rocking their vintage white look against the Washington Commanders for the final time this season.

articles.headline: Jack Grealish issues public apology after making Everton comeback in friendly
articles.description: Jack Grealish has issued a public apology to Everton fans after he made his comeback in a behind-closed-doors match with Derby.
articles.headlineJa: ジャック・グリーリッシュ、親善試合でのエヴァートン復帰後、公に謝罪
articles.descriptionJa: ジャック・グリーリッシュは、ダービーとの非公開試合で復帰したことを受け、エヴァートンのファンに向けて公に謝罪した。
articles.body:
Jack Grealish has issued a public apology to Everton fans after he made his comeback in a behind-closed-doors match with Derby.

Grealish has missed four matches and not played for Everton since Oct. 17 following a breach of club discipline.

Boss David Moyes has been reluctant to discuss any finer details and the club only confirmed the 31-year-old former England winger was "not match-fit" ahead of a trip to Newcastle on Nov. 2.

But Grealish featured in a friendly at Hill Dickinson Stadium on Thursday in the strongest suggestion yet that a line has been drawn over the issue.

"Nice to be back out there with the boys today after a few good days training," Grealish wrote on his Instagram story.

"I want to apologise to the fans and everyone at the club for not being able to help the team the last few weeks.

- Michael Carrick sacked by Man United; sources say Mauricio Pochettino close

- England mark Harry Kane's night with a win, but defence remains a concern

- Italy beat France at home for first time since '62, hand Zidane 1st loss

"I love playing for this club and can't wait to be back playing in front of you guys in an Everton shirt. See you all soon."

Grealish spent the first half of the 2025-26 campaign on loan at Everton before injury curtailed his spell on Merseyside, but he returned on another temporary deal on transfer deadline day.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Liverpool eye move for Brentford's Diouf
articles.description: Could Brentford's El Hadji Malick Diouf be the latest signing at Anfield? Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Liverpool are interested in Brentford full back El Hadji Malick Diouf, while AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott has caught the eye of Arsenal, Chelsea and Liverpool. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Liverpool are interested in Brentford full back El Hadji Malick Diouf, Football Insider reports. The Reds are keen to strengthen on the left side of their defense in January amid concerns over the consistency over Milos Kerkez, and the 21-year-old Senegal international is one of the options being monitored despite the fact it could be difficult to persuade the Bees to part ways with him. Diouf arrived at the club from West Ham United for a fee of around £40 million in the summer.

- Arsenal will challenge Chelsea and Liverpool for the signing of AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott, according to iNews. The Gunners are the latest of the three clubs to make an inquiry about the 23-year-old ahead of a possible move in January, when it is thought an offer worth £80m would be enough for the Cherries to enter formal negotiations. Scott has indicated that he is unwilling to extend his stay at the Vitality Stadium, which makes the upcoming transfer window one of the final opportunities for him to be moved on for the highest possible fee.

- Napoli are tracking Chelsea winger Jamie Gittens amid plans to reinforce their forward line in the next transfer window, according to Corriere dello Sport. Gittens, 22, is being considered as a loan option and is among several players that the Serie A club could approach following a disappointing start to the season, in which they are currently 10th in the league table. He has made just two appearances for the Blues this season.

- Barcelona are interested in FC Twente defender Ruud Nijstad, Diario Sport reports. Barcleona sporting director Deco has already begun work on a move for the 18-year-old as the Blaugrana look to land a left-footed defender with strong ball-playing ability, though the Eredivisie side are set to demand a proposal worth €20m before agreeing to a deal. Nijstad was recently called up to Netherlands' U21 squad.

- PSV Eindhoven have made an inquiry for Napoli midfielder Kevin De Bruyne, according to Nicolò Schira. It is reported that the 35-year-old could leave the Serie A club in the next few months, with PSV checking on his situation ahead of an approach in January. De Bruyne's deal is set to expire next summer, but there is an option clause that would allow Gli Azzurri to extend it by a further year.

articles.headline: Paul Scholes: Mauricio Pochettino has the 'presence' to be Man United boss
articles.description: Paul Scholes believes Mauricio Pochettino is the right man to take over at Manchester United but is concerned they may have missed out on his best years
articles.body:
Paul Scholes believes Mauricio Pochettino is the right man to take over at Manchester United but is concerned they may have missed out on his best years.

Michael Carrick was sacked by United after winning just three of his 15 games in charge this season -- United's worst start to a domestic campaign since 1986.

Carrick took charge of training on Tuesday and Wednesday following the club's dramatic come-from-behind 4-4 draw with Aston Villa on Sunday but was finally relieved of his duties on Thursday.

Manchester United are now looking to appoint former Tottenham and Chelsea boss Pochettino, who is currently head coach of the United States, to succeed Carrick.

Pochettino guided Tottenham to a Champions League final in 2019 and took over at Paris St-Germain where he won the league and cup, but former United midfielder Scholes thinks United may have left it too late to appoint the Argentine.

He told The Good, The Bad and The Football podcast: "I think he's got the presence to manage a big football club like Manchester United. My only slight concern is they have come a little bit too late to the party.

"Mauricio Pochettino is a great manager. I just have that slight concern that we're not getting his best years.

"He's got a bit of a reputation of being a bridesmaid, not winning that many trophies. That possibly put Man Utd off a little bit in the past. They are in a totally different position now."

Pochettino's could be in charge for Manchester United's first game following the international break when they travel to Anfield to face rivals Liverpool next Sunday.

Nicky Butt believes the 54-year-old will have to get some players out of the squad in the January transfer window.

He added: "He's got to work out the ones he can trust, the ones he can't and quickly and get them out in January, he can't stick with that team until next season.

"Manchester United are that low down, they don't even need to think about winning anything at the minute."

Carrick led United to a third place finish last season having stepped in following Ruben Amorim's January exit and was rewarded with a two-year deal.

But Scholes believes he should never have got the job.

articles.headline: Reaction as Man United sack Michael Carrick as manager
articles.description: Manchester United have sacked manager Michael Carrick after a poor run of results. Catch up on the latest reaction to the news.
articles.body:
Michael Carrick was sacked as Manchester United head coach on Thursday after the club dropped into the Premier League relegation zone (18th) with just one league win in 10 games (five draws, four losses) -- their worst-ever start to a league season.

A rollercoaster 4-4 draw was saved late at Old Trafford against Aston Villa at the weekend, and came after a 3-2 win from 2-0 down against Roma in the UEFA Champions League in midweek, but it was not enough to save Carrick from the sack.

United States coach Mauricio Pochettino is the favored candidate to replace Carrick, with the United hierarchy -- led by co-chairman Joel Glazer, minority owner Jim Ratcliffe, CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox -- assessing options in the coming days.

articles.headline: Barcelona fan for life -- and beyond: Fans can pay to deposit ashes at Camp Nou
articles.description: Barcelona are giving their fans the possibility to be part of the club once they pass away by offering from 2027 a columbarium and commemorative plaques at their stadium.
articles.body:
Barcelona are giving their fans the possibility to be part of the club once they pass away by offering from 2027 a columbarium and commemorative plaques at their stadium.

As part of the upgrade to Camp Nou, Barça will have a 1,500m² Memorial space consisting of commemorative plaques and 26,000 niches, where fans' ashes can be deposited.

Both the columbarium and commemorative plaques come with concessions lasting for 10, 25 or 50-year periods. Both options are available to Barça fans worldwide as there is no need to be a club member.

"Two ways of paying tribute and showing remembrance will be available through placing a loved one's ashes in a columbarium or writing a name and message on a commemorative plaque in the Stadium. Both options are available to FC Barcelona fans worldwide, there is no need to be a member," a club statement said.

A peaceful resting place at the Camp Nou will cost from €2,490 ($2,762) for a 10-year concession while the 50-year concession will set you back €5,990 ($6,644). In addition, there is a maintenance fee of €70 per year. A standard 10-year plaque is €490 while a 50-year premium one is €1,040.

Designed by architect Quique Montoya, the Memorial space will combine "fine materials, warm lighting and a contemporary style, with large murals dedicated to notable moments in Barça's history, plus visual, audiovisual and sound elements."

The work, which is being carried out in two phases, will be completed in mid-2028.

"Many fans, members and those with a past at the Club have shown interest in the FC Barcelona Memorial since the launch of the project," the club said.

"These include several former players and relatives of historic figures at Barça who have shown their desire to form part of the initiative."
